identity.fantasy: A lunar battle-priest who turns star generation and consumption into nearby healing, flowing between attacks, Moonwater, prayers, and celestial phases.
identity.one_line: A damage-assisted healer in which consuming Scattered Stars heals nearby allies. Moonflow, Prayer of Elune, Moonwater, Lunar Cascade, and Celestial Form form a mobile critical-healing loop. It can intentionally mix attacks into healing rather than treating damage as incidental.

mechanics.core_loop: Generate Scattered Stars with the appropriate ranged or melee attacks, consume them to heal nearby allies, maintain Moonflow and Moonwater effects, use Prayer of Elune and Mending Surge for direct recovery, and manage mana so short-lived targets do not die before their stars can be consumed.

modes.name: Celestial Form
modes.structural_description: Ascend into a celestial form for 15 seconds, increasing your critical strike chance by 10%.While active, critical strikes now reduce the remaining cooldown of all healing spells by 10% and apply a Scattered Star to your target and up to 4 enemies within 5 yds of them.

mechanics.single_target: Build stars and use direct prayers or Moonwater while converting damage into local healing.
mechanics.aoe: Star consumption, Moonflow, Prayer of Elune, Lunar Cascade, and Rippling Moonwater provide group coverage, but target death before consumption can deny mana and healing value.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Several instant and flowing lunar tools support mobility, yet star marks live on enemies and must be consumed before those targets disappear.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Goddess Watch Over, Lunar Swiftness, slumber, movement healing, and Starcaller defensive tools support a mobile healer.
mechanics.group_utility: Damage, healing, mana cycling, movement support, and Starcaller control make Moon Priest an active hybrid rather than a stationary heal turret.

failure_modes.text: If enemies die before their accumulated stars are consumed, the healer can lose both the expected recovery and the mana cycle needed for the next pull.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: several instant and flowing lunar tools support mobility, yet star marks live on enemies and must be consumed before those targets disappear.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: goddess watch over, lunar swiftness, slumber, movement healing, and starcaller defensive tools support a mobile healer.

praise.theme: Players call Moon Priest engaging, fun, visually strong, capable of meaningful damage, and rewarding when smart choices land.

frustrations.theme: Other players call it poor in leveling dungeons because mobs die before marks can be consumed, causing mana problems.

contested.theme: The same thread describes the spec as both engaging and terrible in dungeons, suggesting group pace and player understanding materially change the experience.

claims.text: A July Moon Priest discussion calls the spec engaging and fun, requiring smart choices and mana management while contributing damage. Another experienced reply calls it poor in leveling dungeons because enemies often die before their stars can be consumed, leaving the healer out of mana unless the group understands the mechanic.
claims.notes: Conflicting reports are preserved because group kill speed plausibly changes the resource cycle.

claims.text: The August Mythic inventory lists 85 Moon Priest records; the community DPS compilation does not list healers and therefore supplies no DPS value.
claims.notes: Upload count is not healing strength.

claims.text: Moon Priest is unusually sensitive to enemy target lifetime because unconsumed stars can withhold both nearby healing and the mana cycle needed for continued casting.
claims.notes: Exact resource return requires live verification.

claims.text: Moon Priest is described as engaging and mana-conscious, but short-lived dungeon targets can die before its marked payoff and produce severe mana pressure without team coordination.
